title: Bill to rename and broaden tobacco control law to cover vaporisers and psychoactive substances
what_it_is: A Bill at Second Reading, moved by Senior Minister of State for Health Dr Koh Poh Koon, to amend the Tobacco (Control of Advertisements and Sale) Act 1993, rename it the Tobacco and Vaporisers Control Act, control vaporisers and specified psychoactive substances, and provide for rehabilitation and penalties.
why_it_matters: The Bill increases the maximum fine for purchase, use and possession of vaporisers from $2,000 to $10,000, and introduces mandatory imprisonment and higher fines for import and supply. It creates rehabilitation orders for people who consume specified psychoactive substances and for repeat vaporiser users, and places duties on owners and occupiers of specified premises and storage spaces. The Senior Minister of State said the Government intends for the Bill to commence on 1 May.

key_points.point: The Government launched a coordinated response to enhance enforcement against vaping on 1 September 2025.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: On 1 September 2025, the Government launched a coordinated response to enhance the enforcement approach towards vaping

key_points.point: Etomidate and its analogues were temporarily listed as Class C controlled drugs under the Misuse of Drugs Act.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: we temporarily listed etomidate and its analogues as Class C controlled drugs in the Misuse of Drugs Act (MDA).

key_points.point: More than 5,100 persons were caught for vaporiser-related offences over the past six months.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: Over the past six months, we have caught more than 5,100 persons for vaporiser-related offences.

key_points.point: More than one in 10 of those caught, or 593, are etomidate vaporiser users.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: Of these, more than one in 10, or 593, are etomidate vaporiser users.

key_points.point: 42 offenders defaulted rehabilitation; one was convicted and imprisoned and the rest will be charged.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: Among the offenders placed on rehabilitation, 42 defaulted their rehabilitation – of which one has been convicted and imprisoned and the rest will be charged.

key_points.point: 70 offenders completed rehabilitation, with four youth offenders re-offending.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: Seventy offenders have completed their rehabilitation programmes, with four youth offenders re-offending after their completion.

key_points.point: The Act is to be renamed the Tobacco and Vaporisers Control Act (TVCA).
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: we are renaming the Tobacco (Control of Advertisements and Sale) Act to the Tobacco and Vaporisers Control Act (TVCA).

key_points.point: The categories of prohibited products under the TVCA are updated.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: we have updated the categories of prohibited products under the TVCA.

key_points.point: Etomidate will be listed in a new Schedule under the TVCA and removed from the MDA.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: Etomidate, currently under the MDA, will be listed in this new Schedule. Concurrently, etomidate will be removed from the MDA.

key_points.point: The Minister for Health can amend the Schedule by order in the Gazette.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: The Minister for Health can amend this Schedule by order in the Gazette.

key_points.point: Supplying SPS products carries two to 10 years imprisonment and two to five strokes of the cane.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: individuals who supply SPS products will face two to 10 years imprisonment term and two to five strokes of the cane.

key_points.point: Importing SPS products carries three to 20 years imprisonment and five to 15 strokes of the cane.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: Those who import these products will face stiffer penalties – three to 20 years imprisonment term and five to 15 strokes of the cane.

key_points.point: Possessing or purchasing SPS products, or consuming SPS, can lead to a fine up to $20,000, imprisonment up to 10 years, or both.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: those caught possessing or purchasing such products, or consuming SPS, if prosecuted, can be liable to a fine of up to $20,000, or imprisonment for up to 10 years, or both.

key_points.point: It will be an offence for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents to consume SPS overseas.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: it will be an offence for Singapore Citizens and Permanent Residents to consume SPS overseas.

key_points.point: Section 19G targets adults who leave SPS products where children can access them or fail to prevent use by young persons.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: Section 19G targets adults who, being in possession of SPS products, first, knowingly or recklessly leave them where children can access them, or second, do not take reasonable steps to prevent the use of SPS products by young persons.

key_points.point: Section 19H addresses adults who involve young or vulnerable persons in importing or supplying SPS products.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: Section 19H addresses adults who involve young or vulnerable persons in importing or supplying SPS products.

key_points.point: Section 19I makes it an offence to arrange or plan gatherings where SPS products are used or supplied.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: Section 19I makes it an offence to arrange or plan gatherings where SPS products are used or supplied.

key_points.point: The Chief Executive of HSA can order community-based rehabilitation and institutional treatment under the TVCA.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: We will now provide for specific powers for the Chief Executive of the Health Sciences Authority (HSA) to order community-based rehabilitation and institutional treatment and rehabilitation under the TVCA.

key_points.point: Rehabilitation will only be ordered for repeat offenders.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: As per our current practice, rehabilitation will only be ordered for repeat offenders, to support them to quit vaping.

key_points.point: The Chief Executive can order institutional treatment and rehabilitation in the DRC for re-offending SPS consumption cases.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: the Chief Executive can also, under section 19U, order institutional treatment and rehabilitation in the DRC, for re-offending cases of SPS consumption.

key_points.point: The maximum fine for purchase, use and possession of vaporisers increases from $2,000 to $10,000.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: For purchase, use and possession, the maximum fine will be increased from $2,000 to $10,000.

key_points.point: Importing vaporisers or section 15 tobacco products carries mandatory imprisonment up to nine years and a possible fine up to $300,000.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: For offences involving the import of vaporisers or section 15 tobacco products, we are introducing mandatory imprisonment for up to nine years, and additionally, offenders may face a fine of up to $300,000.

key_points.point: Sale or supply of these products carries mandatory imprisonment up to six years and a possible fine up to $200,000.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: For offences involving the sale or supply, including possession for the purpose of sale or supply, of these products, offenders will face mandatory imprisonment for up to six years, and additionally, may face a fine of up to $200,000.

key_points.point: Imitation tobacco product offences carry higher fines and imprisonment for first-time and repeat offences.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: For offences involving the sale, supply or import of imitation tobacco products, the penalties will be increased to a fine of up to $100,000, or imprisonment of up to three years, or both for first-time offences; and a fine of up to $200,000, or imprisonment for up to six years, or both for repeat offences.

key_points.point: If vaporisers are found in a vehicle entering Singapore, the driver is presumed to be in possession of them.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: if vaporisers are found in a vehicle entering Singapore, the driver of that vehicle will be presumed to be in possession of the vaporisers, and cannot avoid legal liability by simply claiming ignorance that the vaporisers are present in the vehicle.

key_points.point: Under new section 18A, owners and occupiers commit an offence if they allow storage of prohibited products in their spaces.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: Under the new section 18A, introduced by clause 10, it is an offence for owners and occupiers of land, buildings and places to allow other individuals to store prohibited products in these spaces.

key_points.point: HSA will publish a handbook of best practices for owners and occupiers.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: HSA will publish a handbook of best practices that owners and occupiers can refer to.

key_points.point: New powers allow seizure of vehicles, trailers and cash suspected to be connected to a TVCA offence.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: we are also introducing new powers to seize vehicles and trailers reasonably suspected of being used, or is intended to be used in connection with committing an offence under the TVCA, and to seize cash that is reasonably suspected to be evidence that a TVCA offence has been committed.

key_points.point: Specified premises initially include discotheques, pubs, bars, lounges and night clubs.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: As a start, specified premises will include discotheques, pubs, bars, lounges and night clubs.

key_points.point: Related and consequential amendments are made to the Poisons Act, MDA, Civil Defence Act, Merchant Shipping Act and Road Traffic Act.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: There are several related and consequential amendments to several other pieces of legislation, such as the Poisons Act, MDA, Civil Defence Act, Merchant Shipping Act, and Road Traffic Act, to align to the TVCA.

key_points.point: The Government intends for the Bill to commence on 1 May.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: We intend for the Bill to commence on 1 May and will provide support to responsible persons and owners and occupiers before then.

key_points.point: Mr Yip Hon Weng supports the Bill.
key_points.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
key_points.quote: I support this Bill.

key_points.point: Mr Yip Hon Weng asks what charging guidance will distinguish deliberate abuse from peer pressure or deception.
key_points.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
key_points.quote: What charging guidance will distinguish deliberate abuse from peer pressure or deception?

key_points.point: Mr Yip Hon Weng asks what percentage reduction in youth cases is targeted within 12 to 24 months.
key_points.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
key_points.quote: What percentage reduction in youth cases is targeted within 12 to 24 months?

key_points.point: Mr Yip Hon Weng asks whether offences under the Act will be treated as spent after a period.
key_points.speaker: Mr Yip Hon Weng
key_points.quote: Will offences under this Act be treated as spent after a period?

key_points.point: Ms He Ting Ru hopes enforcement gives users the opportunity to turn over a new leaf instead of stigmatising them.
key_points.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
key_points.quote: I hope that enforcement efforts will provide users the opportunity to turn over a new leaf instead of inadvertently stigmatising them.

key_points.point: Ms He Ting Ru repeats the call to consider a tobacco cohort ban.
key_points.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
key_points.quote: I therefore repeat our call to consider instituting a tobacco cohort ban.

key_points.point: Ms He Ting Ru notes tobacco excise duties increased by 20% from 49.1 cents to 58.9 cents per cigarette.
key_points.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
key_points.quote: tobacco excise duties were increased by 20% from 49.1 cents to 58.9 cents per cigarette.

key_points.point: Ms He Ting Ru notes the smoking rate has dropped to an all-time low of 8.4%.
key_points.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
key_points.quote: Our smoking rate has dropped to an all-time low of 8.4%

key_points.point: Dr Hamid Razak supports the Bill.
key_points.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak
key_points.quote: I rise in support of this Bill.

key_points.point: Dr Hamid Razak asks how the Ministry will ensure preventive education and health literacy.
key_points.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak
key_points.quote: how the Ministry will ensure that there is preventive education and health literacy alongside and in a strong way?

key_points.point: Dr Hamid Razak asks whether there will be an increase in training supervising officers.
key_points.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak
key_points.quote: Will there be an increase in training supervising officers?

key_points.point: Dr Hamid Razak asks what operational guidance will be provided.
key_points.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak
key_points.quote: what operational guidance will be provided.

key_points.point: Dr Hamid Razak asks how enforcement agencies will distinguish between devices and substances under the TVCA and MDA.
key_points.speaker: Dr Hamid Razak
key_points.quote: how will enforcement agencies operationally distinguish between these categories of devices and substances

key_points.point: Mr Gerald Giam supports the amendments controlling purchase, use, possession, import and supply of vaporisers and SPS.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam
key_points.quote: I support the amendments in this Bill, which control the purchase, use, possession, import and supply of vaporisers and specified psychoactive substances.

key_points.point: Mr Gerald Giam reiterates his call for a cohort tobacco ban.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam
key_points.quote: I reiterate my call from 5 March 2024 and echo my hon friend, Ms He Ting Ru, regarding a cohort tobacco ban.

key_points.point: Mr Gerald Giam asks what nicotine yield limit the Senior Minister of State intends to prescribe under new section 14.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam
key_points.quote: Can I ask the Senior Minister of State what nicotine yield limit he intends to prescribe for this for Singapore under the new section 14?

key_points.point: Mr Gerald Giam urges the Minister to use clause 21 powers to set standards for tobacco product use and emissions to address second-hand smoke.
key_points.speaker: Mr Gerald Giam
key_points.quote: I urge the Minister to utilise the powers under clause 21 to set standards for the use and emissions of tobacco products, ensuring that private enjoyment does not result in the involuntary consumption of secondary emissions by neighbours.

key_points.point: Dr Choo Pei Ling supports the Bill.
key_points.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling
key_points.quote: I rise in strong support of the Bill.

key_points.point: Dr Choo Pei Ling says expanding definitions to capture nicotine analogues and creating the SPS framework ensures enforcement can respond swiftly.
key_points.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling
key_points.quote: The expansion of definitions to capture nicotine analogues and the creation of a Specified Psychoactive Substances framework ensure that enforcement can respond swiftly as substances evolve.

key_points.point: Dr Choo Pei Ling asks how agencies will prioritise dismantling organised supply networks and measure disruption.
key_points.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling
key_points.quote: I would welcome the Senior Minister of State’s clarification on how agencies will prioritise dismantling organised supply networks and measure disruption of these channels

key_points.point: Dr Choo Pei Ling asks how diversion to rehabilitation will be operationalised quickly.
key_points.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling
key_points.quote: I would be grateful if the Minister could elaborate on how agencies will ensure that diversion to rehabilitation is operationalised quickly

key_points.point: Dr Neo Kok Beng supports the Bill.
key_points.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng
key_points.quote: I rise to support the Bill.

key_points.point: Dr Neo Kok Beng asks about the current situation of peddling vapes to students and youths.
key_points.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng
key_points.quote: What is the current situation of the peddling of vapes or vaporiser who are getting the students and our youths?

key_points.point: Dr Neo Kok Beng asks what educational and awareness programmes for students will be provided.
key_points.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng
key_points.quote: what are the educational and awareness programmes for students going forward?

key_points.point: Dr Neo Kok Beng asks whether parents will be given tools to identify vaping devices and potential use by their child.
key_points.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng
key_points.quote: is there any plan to equip or provide parents with tools for them to identify vaping devices and the potential use or identify the potential use of vapes by the child?

key_points.point: Dr Neo Kok Beng asks whether there are plans to install vape detection systems in IHL campuses and hostels.
key_points.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng
key_points.quote: do we have plans to install vapes detection systems in the IHL campus and hostels?

key_points.point: Dr Wan Rizal strongly supports the measures.
key_points.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
key_points.quote: I strongly support these measures.

key_points.point: Dr Wan Rizal asks how enforcement agencies will operationalise strengthened provisions in complex supply environments.
key_points.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
key_points.quote: I would like to seek clarification on how enforcement agencies intend to operationalise these strengthened provisions in increasingly complex supply environments, including decentralised storage and informal distribution channels.

key_points.point: Dr Wan Rizal asks about projected caseload, supervising officer capacity, addiction-trained clinicians and relapse prevention.
key_points.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
key_points.quote: I would like to seek clarification on firstly, the projected caseload for community-based rehabilitation under Part 3A; secondly, whether the supervising officer's capacity is being expanded; the availability of addiction-trained clinicians and counsellors; and finally, the framework for relapse prevention during and after supervision.

key_points.point: Dr Wan Rizal says storage operators, landlords, transport providers and small business owners seek clarity on due care and reasonable knowledge.
key_points.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
key_points.quote: commercial storage operators, landlords, transport providers and small business owners will understandably seek clarity on what constitutes "due care" and "reasonable knowledge".

key_points.point: Dr Wan Rizal encourages a formal review of the Part 3A framework within three to five years.
key_points.speaker: Dr Wan Rizal
key_points.quote: I would encourage the Ministry to consider a formal review of the Part 3A framework within three to five years of implementation.

key_points.point: Ms Kuah Boon Theng supports the Bill.
key_points.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng
key_points.quote: I rise in support of this Bill.

key_points.point: Ms Kuah Boon Theng notes more than 3,000 students were caught vaping every year between 2022 and 2024.
key_points.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng
key_points.quote: More than 3,000 students were caught vaping every year between 2022 and 2024.

key_points.point: Ms Kuah Boon Theng asks whether there will be close collaboration with parents and schools for youth vape users.
key_points.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng
key_points.quote: will there be any close collaboration or coordination with parents and schools to implement a structured programme or protocol to help them kick the habit?

key_points.point: Ms Kuah Boon Theng proposes a national protocol team of child and adolescent psychiatrists, addiction specialists and counsellors.
key_points.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng
key_points.quote: I would therefore like to propose that MOH consider assembling a team of child and adolescent psychiatrists, qualified addiction specialists and professional counsellors, to come up with a national protocol or programme

key_points.point: Ms Kuah Boon Theng asks if the Ministry intends to track data of young vape users who are minors.
key_points.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng
key_points.quote: I would like to ask the Senior Minister of State if the Ministry intends to track the data of young vape users who are minors

key_points.point: Mr Vikram Nair supports the Bill.
key_points.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
key_points.quote: I support this Bill.

key_points.point: Mr Vikram Nair notes the Bill reclassifies etomidate from a Class C controlled drug under the MDA to a specified psychoactive substance under the TVCA.
key_points.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
key_points.quote: The current Bill provides for the reclassification of etomidate from a Class C controlled drug under the MDA to a "specified psychoactive substance" under the proposed TVCA.

key_points.point: Mr Vikram Nair asks what considerations determine whether a psychoactive substance is listed under the TVCA.
key_points.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
key_points.quote: what considerations will determine whether a psychoactive substance is to be listed under the TVCA?

key_points.point: Mr Vikram Nair asks whether a case can be caught by both the TVCA and MDA and how prosecution is decided.
key_points.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
key_points.quote: is it possible for a case to be caught by both the TVCA and the MDA, and if so, how will the authorities decide which statute to prosecute an offender under?

key_points.point: Mr Vikram Nair asks whether sentencing guidelines and cases under the MDA apply to TVCA cases.
key_points.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
key_points.quote: will sentencing guidelines and cases under the MDA apply to cases under the TVCA?

key_points.point: Mr Vikram Nair asks what happens if more harmful drugs are found during an HSA raid for vaporisers or etomidate.
key_points.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
key_points.quote: what happens if more harmful substances or drugs are found while the HSA is conducting a raid for vaporisers and/or etomidate?

key_points.point: Mr Vikram Nair asks whether offenders subject to mandatory treatment will be sent to existing DRCs or different facilities.
key_points.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
key_points.quote: would offenders subject to mandatory treatment under this Bill be sent to DRCs currently used for drug offenders or is the intention to send them to different facilities?

key_points.point: Mr Vikram Nair asks how overlap between HSA and CNB rehabilitation orders will be resolved.
key_points.speaker: Mr Vikram Nair
key_points.quote: how will this overlap be resolved between the HSA and the CNB?

key_points.point: Dr Koh Poh Koon says firm enforcement alone will never eliminate vaping.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: firm enforcement alone will never eliminate vaping.

key_points.point: Dr Koh Poh Koon says vaping is not yet deeply entrenched and there is a critical window to act.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: Vaping has not yet become deeply entrenched in Singapore. This gives us a critical window to act decisively.

key_points.point: Dr Koh Poh Koon describes the national campaign across multiple platforms, including digital display panels, mainstream media and social media.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: The national campaign across multiple platforms includes digital display panels cross the island, in our heartlands, especially, mainstream media and social media to inform the public about the dangers of vaping and etomidate vaporisers.

key_points.point: Dr Koh Poh Koon says those who come forward voluntarily to quit will not be penalised, and more than 110 persons came forward to quit etomidate vaping in the past six months.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: Those who come forward voluntarily will not be penalised for doing so. In the past six months, more than 110 persons came forward to quit etomidate vaping.

key_points.point: Dr Koh Poh Koon says students caught for the first time will be guided by school counsellors and referred to HPB's QuitLine when needed.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: students caught for the first time will be guided by school counsellors and referred to the Health Promotion Board's (HPB's) QuitLine when needed.

key_points.point: Dr Koh Poh Koon says the Youth Enhanced Supervision Scheme for youths under 21 includes family involvement.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: For youths under 21 years old, the Youth Enhanced Supervision Scheme under the Ministry of Social and Family Development has an added element of family involvement, with some sessions conducted together with their parents or guardians.

key_points.point: Dr Koh Poh Koon says parents can refer to the Parent's Guide on Vaping on the Families for Life website.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: Parents can also refer to the Parent's Guide on Vaping on the Families for Life website for tips on having conversations with their children on vaping.

key_points.point: Dr Koh Poh Koon says parents who refuse to be involved in their children's counselling without reasonable justification may face criminal charges.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: Parents who refuse to be involved in their children's counselling without reasonable justifications will potentially face criminal charges.

key_points.point: Dr Koh Poh Koon says vaping re-offenders will be prosecuted and subject to the increased fine up to $10,000.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: For vaping, they will be prosecuted and subject to the increased fine, up to $10,000.

key_points.point: Dr Koh Poh Koon says etomidate vaping re-offenders will be detained in the DRC for institutional treatment and rehabilitation.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: For etomidate vaping, they will be detained in the DRC for institutional treatment and rehabilitation.

key_points.point: Dr Koh Poh Koon says DRC placement will be separate from other drug offenders.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: In answer to Mr Vikram Nair's question, this will be separate from other drug offenders.

key_points.point: Dr Koh Poh Koon says mandatory imprisonment is imposed for importers and suppliers of section 15 tobacco products and vaporisers because they drive continued availability.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: mandatory imprisonment is imposed for importers and suppliers of section 15 tobacco products and vaporisers because they drive the continued availability of these harmful products.

key_points.point: Dr Koh Poh Koon says over 10,000 online advertisements were removed since 2024 and 27 websites blocked under OCHA since September last year.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: Over 10,000 online advertisements were removed since 2024 and 27 websites blocked under the OCHA since September last year.

key_points.point: Dr Koh Poh Koon says joint HSA and ICA operations detected 59 large-scale smuggling cases in 2025, seizing around 230,000 vaporisers and related products, with 13 charged.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: joint operations by HSA and ICA detected 59 large-scale smuggling cases in 2025, seizing around 230,000 vaporisers and related products. Thirteen of these cases have been charged.

key_points.point: Dr Koh Poh Koon says an SPS scheduled under the TVCA is automatically excluded from the MDA psychoactive substances framework.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: A SPS, once scheduled under the TVCA, will be automatically excluded from the framework of psychoactive substances under the MDA

key_points.point: Dr Koh Poh Koon says if both SPS and MDA-controlled drugs are consumed, the MDA rehabilitation framework takes precedence.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: If both SPS and controlled drugs or psychoactive substances under the MDA are consumed, the MDA rehabilitation framework will take precedence

key_points.point: Dr Koh Poh Koon says HSA and CNB will investigate jointly if necessary, and the Attorney-General's Chambers makes the ultimate prosecution decision.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: HSA and CNB will investigate the cases jointly if necessary. The ultimate decision on prosecution will be made by the Attorney-General's Chambers.

key_points.point: Dr Koh Poh Koon says HSA will publish a handbook of best practices today on its website to illustrate due care for owners and occupiers.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: HSA will publish a handbook of best practices today on their website to illustrate what constitutes "due care" by owners and occupiers of land, buildings and places under the new offence of allowing other individuals to store prohibited products or their components in these spaces.

key_points.point: Dr Koh Poh Koon says a whole-of-Government enforcement approach involves Police, CNB, NEA and NParks assisting in detection and referral to HSA.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: We adopted a whole-of-Government enforcement approach, where relevant agencies, such as the Police, CNB, NEA and National Parks Board (NParks) assist in the detection and referral of suspected cases to HSA.

key_points.point: Dr Koh Poh Koon says more than 13,000 officers are authorised to-date, multiplying effective enforcement capacity.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: This has multiplied our effective enforcement capacity, with more than 13,000 officers authorised to-date.

key_points.point: Dr Koh Poh Koon says sufficient rehabilitation capacity, including in the DRC, has been provided and will be regularly reviewed.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: On rehabilitation capacity, having operated these programmes for the past six months, we have provided for sufficient capacity, including in the DRC.

key_points.point: Dr Koh Poh Koon says MHA works with international and regional partners to monitor new psychoactive substances.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: MHA already works with international and regional partners, such as the Commission on Narcotic Drugs, the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime and the Association of Southeast Asia Nations (ASEAN) counterparts, to monitor the emergence of new psychoactive substances.

key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: HSA also collects and exchanges intelligence with the World Health Organization and international regulatory counterparts and, on our own, we conduct random testing of vaporisers that we have seized to detect any new substances that is emerging in our market.

key_points.point: Dr Koh Poh Koon says a new psychoactive substance can be listed in the TVCA Schedule quickly by order in the Gazette.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: If another psychoactive substance or product emerges in tobacco products, vaporisers or imitation tobacco products, it can be listed in the Schedule of TVCA fairly quickly, by amending the Schedule via an order in the Gazette made by the Minister for Health.

key_points.point: Dr Koh Poh Koon clarifies that clause 37 is an amendment to NEA's Smoking (Prohibition in Certain Places) Act, not the Tobacco Control Act.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: Let me clarify that this is actually an amendment to the Ministry of Sustainability and the Environment (MSE)/NEA's smoking prohibition on certain places. It is not for the Tobacco Control Act, but it is actually an amendment to NEA's Smoking (Prohibition in Certain Places) Act.

key_points.point: Dr Koh Poh Koon says existing limits on nicotine and tar content emission of cigarettes continue under the TVCA.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: We have existing limits on the content emission of nicotine and tar of cigarettes that will continue under the TVCA.

key_points.point: Dr Koh Poh Koon says Singapore's nicotine emission yield has been capped at 1.0 milligrams since 2013.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: in Singapore, our nicotine emission yield is also capped at 1.0 milligrams since 2013.

key_points.point: Dr Koh Poh Koon says the Government will work with NEA and MSE on the suggestion to manage second-hand smoke and smoking in heartlands.
key_points.speaker: Dr Koh Poh Koon
key_points.quote: We will work with NEA and MSE on the Member of Parliament's suggestion to see how we can continue to help manage the issue of second-hand smoke and smoking within our heartlands.

what_happens_next: The Deputy Speaker said that if there are no clarifications arising from the Senior Minister of State's response, he will put the question to the House. The Senior Minister of State said the Government intends for the Bill to commence on 1 May.
